Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Discrepancy on April invoice + temporary CCPA data hold

Hi Kimberly,

We received our April invoice (attached) and the usage line for API tokens is ~38% above our expectation compared to April last year. The spike looks concentrated around three days (Apr 13–15) and maps to a large ingestion job we started, but the numbers don't reconcile with our internal telemetry.

Before we escalate to procurement for a formal dispute, two asks: 1) can Redwood provide a session-level crosswalk or a small usage sample for Apr 13–15 so we can match request IDs? 2) Veridian is initiating a temporary CCPA data hold for that ingestion window — we may need any PII-related logs/redaction confirmation from Redwood while the hold is in effect.

Attachments: invoice_20270430.pdf (pdf)

Thanks,
Elena Ruiz
Director, Finance Operations
Veridian Health

Elena — thanks for flagging this and for the heads up on the CCPA hold. We're pulling the token-level evidence now. Quick notes:

- We'll provide a small redacted usage sample (request IDs only, no payloads) for Apr 13–15 so your team can match against request ids.
- If you need redaction confirmation or attestations related to PII handling, that will require coordination with our Privacy team; I can loop them in after the sample is validated.
- Ben will run a preliminary attribution check for duplicate ingestion and session split/merge edge cases; Connor can scope any provisional credit while we investigate.

I'll send the sample CSV within 24 hours and a short write-up of our initial findings. For now, please confirm the HubSpot deal id (D-4721) is the correct record for this billing conversation.

Best,

Kimberly / Connor — attaching the redacted sample and a short crosswalk. Key observations:

1) sample_usage_window.csv (attached) — contains request_id, timestamp_utc, model, token_count, route_id. All PII fields redacted per Elena's request.
2) There are ~2.3k request_ids in the Apr 13–15 window with identical user_agent and IP fingerprint; after digging we discovered a job that re-played a subset of requests with a different tenant tag which caused double attribution in our session-merging logic.
3) Root cause: tenant-tag mismatch on a retrying ingest client + a race in our session attribution when request metadata changed mid-stream. This produced duplicated token attributions for ~5% of the window and inflated the billed token count.

Next steps proposed:
- We can issue a provisional credit equal to the duplicated-attribution tokens while we complete a full ledger replay (est. 72 hours).
- We'll provide an attestation letter from our Privacy team confirming no payloads or PII were included in the sample and that logs accessed for the crosswalk are retained according to our retention policy.
- Engineering will schedule a short patch to harden session attribution for tenant-tag changes; ETA two weeks.

Attachments: sample_usage_window.csv, provisional_credit_calc.xlsx

Ben Carter
Billing & Metering Specialist, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 17:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Discrepancy on April invoice + temporary CCPA data hold

Elena — thanks for your patience. Quick summary and proposed resolution:

- We've validated Ben's initial finding. The preliminary replay suggests ~4.9% of Apr 13–15 billed tokens are attributable to duplicate attribution. The attached provisional_credit_calc.xlsx shows the credit math and the provisional invoice adjustment.
- Because you're initiating a CCPA hold, our Privacy team (privacy@redwood.com) confirms we only shared request identifiers and other non-payload metadata in the sample; we'll produce a short attestation letter by EOD Monday.
- Proposed immediate action: apply a provisional credit for the duplicated tokens to your May 7 statement (or issue a one-off credit note if you prefer). We'll finalize the credit after a full ledger replay (target completion: Tue 24 May).

Please confirm you want the provisional credit applied now or whether procurement should wait for the final reconciliation. If you need a formal amendment or DocuSign for the credit note, we'll generate it once you confirm.

Thanks,
Connor O'Brien
Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference
